author: Magnolia State News
title: Conehatta man admits guilt in sexual abuse case involving minor
text:
Patrick Lemon Acting United States Attorney for the Southern District of Mississippi | Department of Justice
Patrick Lemon Acting United States Attorney for the Southern District of Mississippi | Department of Justice
A man from Newton County has admitted guilt in a case involving the sexual abuse of a minor. Javeon Deshaun Jefferson, aged 25, entered his plea on June 17, 2025. The incident occurred in February 2024 within the Conehatta Community of the Choctaw Indian Reservation.
Acting U.S. Attorney Patrick A. Lemon of the Southern District of Mississippi announced the development. The investigation was conducted by both the Choctaw Police Department and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
Jefferson is set to receive his sentence on October 28, 2025. He could face up to fifteen years in prison, although a federal district judge will make the final decision based on U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other legal considerations.
The prosecution was handled by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kevin J. Payne and Brian K. Burns.
